taskVersion.name: deadline-math-pairs-direct
taskVersion.description: Pre-registered paired set, answer-only mode. 50 trap/control pairs: the same deadline inside and outside the weeks when the EU and US change clocks on different dates, and durations that do or do not cross a clock change. Ground truth from zoneinfo.

parts.text:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close Monday, October 26, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? Reply with exactly one line and nothing else: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert from PT (Pacific Time) to Madrid time on October 26, 2026.

October 26, 2026: PT is PDT (UTC-7) since US daylight saving time ends first Sunday of November.

Madrid in late October: CET (UTC+1) since Europe's DST ends last Sunday of October. In 2026, the last Sunday of October is October 25. So on October 26, Madrid is on CET (UTC+1).

PT (PDT) = UTC-7, Madrid = UTC+1, difference = +8 hours.

October 26, 11:59 PM PT → October 27, 07:59 AM Madrid time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-27 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close Monday, October 19, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? Reply with exactly one line and nothing else: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert from PT (Pacific Time) to Madrid time.

October 19, 2026: PT is PDT (UTC-7), and Madrid is CEST (UTC+2) — wait, let me check. In October, DST in Europe ends the last Sunday of October. In 2026, the last Sunday of October is October 25. So on October 19, Madrid is still on CEST (UTC+2).

PDT = UTC-7, so 11:59 PM PDT = 06:59 UTC on October 20.
Madrid (UTC+2): 06:59 + 2 = 08:59 on October 20, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-20 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close Tuesday, October 27, 2026 at 9:00 AM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? Reply with exactly one line and nothing else: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Spain (Madrid) is in the CET/CEST timezone. In October 2026, daylight saving time ends on the last Sunday of October, which is October 25, 2026. So on October 27, 2026, Spain is on CET (UTC+1).

PT (Pacific Time) on October 27, 2026: The US ends DST on November 1, 2026, so PT is still PDT (UTC-7) on October 27.

Offset: CET (UTC+1) vs PDT (UTC-7) = +8 hours.

9:00 AM PDT + 8 hours = 17:00 CET.

ANSWER: 2026-10-27 17:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close Tuesday, October 20, 2026 at 9:00 AM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? Reply with exactly one line and nothing else: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to determine the UTC offset for Madrid on October 20, 2026.

Madrid uses CET (UTC+1) in winter and CEST (UTC+2) in summer. In 2026, Europe switches from CEST to CET on the last Sunday of October, which is October 25, 2026. So on October 20, 2026, Madrid is still on CEST (UTC+2).

PT on October 20, 2026: The US switches from PDT to PST on the first Sunday of November, so October 20 is still PDT (UTC-7).

Convert 9:00 AM PDT to UTC: 9:00 + 7 = 16:00 UTC
Convert 16:00 UTC to Madrid (CEST, UTC+2): 16:00 + 2 = 18:00

ANSWER: 2026-10-20 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close Wednesday, October 28, 2026 at 5:00 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? Reply with exactly one line and nothing else: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to determine Madrid's UTC offset on October 28, 2026.

Spain (Madrid) observes CET (UTC+1) in winter and CEST (UTC+2) in summer. The EU clocks change on the last Sunday of October. In 2026, October's last Sunday is October 25, so Madrid switches from CEST (UTC+2) to CET (UTC+1) on October 25. By October 28, Madrid is on CET = UTC+1.

PT on October 28, 2026: The US clocks fall back on the first Sunday of November. In 2026, that's November 1. So on October 28, PT is still PDT = UTC-7.

5:00 PM PDT = 17:00 UTC-7 = 00:00 UTC (next day, October 29).

00:00 UTC+1 = 01:00 on October 29 in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 01:00

Convert UTC 00:00 October 22 to Madrid (UTC+2): 02:00 on October 22, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-22 02:00
